# Deep Learning 2026: Project Overview

This project involves the implementation of a published deep learning architecture using PyTorch, which must be developed entirely from scratch. Students are required to use external resources, including ChatGPT, only for gaining a deeper understanding of the architecture, and not for copying any code. Once implemented, the architecture should be tested on a relevant dataset.

## Key Dates:

The evaluation of the project will occur approximately two weeks after the course concludes, which is expected to be around the first week of December.

## Architecture Selection:

Students must choose an "advanced" architecture related to one or two course topics. The options include either selecting from a predefined list (below) or proposing an alternative architecture. Any proposals for alternate architectures must be submitted before the end of the course.

Considering the complexity of these architectures and potential computational constraints, students may simplify the project at the dataset or hyperparameter level.

## List of Valid Architectures:

    [Vision + XAI]: ProtoPNet (paper link) or PIPNet (paper link) with either the CUB or CARS dataset
    [Vision + XAI]: Concept Whitening for Interpretable Image Recognition (paper link)

    [Vision + Generative]: Diffusion GAN (paper link) applied to a dataset of your choice

    [Vision + Unsupervised]: CUTS (paper link) with one of the three datasets referenced in the paper

    [Diffusion + XAI]: Self-Discovering Interpretable Diffusion Latent Directions for Responsible Text-to-Image Generation (paper link)

    [Multimodal Transformer]: LXMERT: Learning Cross-Modality Encoder Representations from Transformers (paper link)

## Report Requirements:

A minimum 2-page report must accompany the project, including:

    - An explanation of the selected architecture and a brief literature review.
    - Details of the dataset(s) used.
    - A summary of any experiments conducted.
    - A description of the simplifications made (if any) and the reasoning behind them.

## Group Work:

The project can be completed individually or in groups of up to 3 students.

## Delivery:

The project report should be delivered at least two days before the presentation in an assignment box on moodle and the code should be uploaded on a github repository.
